question: Does a per-root identity partition for shadow content earn its cost in wall time?

arms.base: same bundle, __styleShareShadowRootTwins:false — released behavior, shadow content reads in full
arms.opt: same bundle, __styleShareShadowRootTwins:true — the CEILING spike: per-root identity token, no per-root sheet scan

ceiling: The opt arm is deliberately the cheapest thing that could capture the whole win, and it is deliberately unsound on a root whose own sheet splits twins. A sound partition needs a per-root scan on top, so the opt arm measures an UPPER BOUND on the win and the sound build can only be smaller. That is what makes a sub-threshold result falsifying rather than merely discouraging.

decision.promoteToDesign: Every splitting-free shadow fixture clears minEffectPct with a clean instrument AND the no-op control is equivalent AND no fixture regresses.
decision.reject: No shadow fixture's 95% CI upper bound reaches minEffectPct, OR the instrument is noisy on any fixture, OR the no-op control is not equivalent, OR any fixture regresses by more than minEffectPct.
decision.incomplete: A blocked ambient gate, a missing matrix cell, provenance drift, a missing report or an unparseable report. Zero evidence can never look like a promising partition.
decision.note: A rejection is a settled question, not a retry with more replicates. Only a promoteToDesign result authorizes building the sound per-root partition, and promoteToDesign is still not a promotion to production.

purpose: Falsifier. This policy can reject the per-root partition or authorize DESIGNING it. It can never promote it.
